findings.issue_category: KMS key policy grants wildcard principals
findings.description: The key has no `policy` argument, so it falls back to the default key policy, which grants `kms:*` on `Resource: "*"` to the entire account (via the account principal), and this is a KMS key that receives CloudTrail/audit data. Any principal in the account that is granted kms permissions by an IAM policy can use it, and if account-level access was ever broadened (or if this key protects a log bucket), a single over-permissive IAM policy yields decrypt of the audit trail. An explicit least-privilege key policy should name only the specific roles/services (e.g. CloudTrail, the log-archive role) that need Encrypt/Decrypt/DescribeKey.
`enable_key_rotation` is not set, so automatic annual rotation is disabled for the key. Failure to enable rotation means a compromised or leaked key material remains valid far longer than necessary.

The key is defined without `is_enabled`/`multi_region`/`deletion_window_in_days` being strengthened beyond the 7-day minimum; the 7-day window is the shortest permitted value, which gives a very short recovery period for an audit-log key if it is destroyed by mistake or by a hostile change. Consider the maximum 30-day window for keys protecting audit data.
